title: Young adults are using ChatGPT to script their in-person conversations. Psychologists call it an “epidemic of self-mistrust.”

content_html:
TL;DR

Young adults are using AI chatbots to draft dating lines, party icebreakers, and real-time in-person responses. Psychologists warn it creates “self-mistrust.” A relationship coach suggests capping AI rehearsal to once a week.

A growing number of young adults are using AI chatbots to script not just their texts but their in-person conversations, the Wall Street Journal reported. Niharika Abbaraju, a 20-year-old cancer researcher, uses ChatGPT at work for research, but off the clock it becomes her conversation coach, drafting dating app lines, party icebreakers, and real-time responses to whoever is standing next to her. When a conversation drifts toward a book she has not read, she pulls up an AI summary to fake her way through it.

She is not alone. The pattern extends across a generation of young adults who let chatbots steer their dating messages and social interactions, particularly those with social anxiety. The results are sometimes obvious: Austin personal trainer Andrea Wallace noticed a date’s texting grammar suddenly improved, a tell. Northwestern student Lucas Dvorak’s girlfriend told him using AI on her felt “creepy.” Kalin Lincoln, 20, uses ChatGPT to cool down angry emails and prep notes before difficult conversations, but says it backfired at least once, giving her the opposite advice she needed.

Clinical psychologist Ashleigh Golden warns that asking AI to check whether your texts “sound okay” quietly teaches you to distrust your own instincts. Mental health professionals call the pattern an “epidemic of self-mistrust.” Relationship coach Alexandra Friedman suggests capping AI rehearsal to once a week and using a chatbot for what to say, never how to say it. Wharton researchers coined “cognitive surrender” to describe people deferring to AI even when it is wrong, and the social version is the same phenomenon applied to personality rather than facts. The AI version of you is more articulate. The in-person version is the one who has to sustain the conversation.

A study found AI advice made people three times less accurate but twice as confident, and the social parallel is precise: outsourcing conversations builds confidence in the script, not in yourself. Every uncomfortable moment avoided is a confidence-building opportunity lost. The chatbot handles the hard part. The anxiety stays exactly where it was.

content_html_zh:
TL;DR

年轻人正在使用人工智能聊天机器人来起草约会路线、派对破冰活动和实时面对面回复。 心理学家警告说，这会造成“自我不信任”。 一位关系教练建议将人工智能排练限制为每周一次。

据《华尔街日报》报道，越来越多的年轻人使用人工智能聊天机器人不仅编写文本，还编写面对面的对话。 Niharika Abbaraju 是一位 20 岁的癌症研究员，她在工作中使用 ChatGPT 进行研究，但在下班后，它成为她的对话教练，起草约会应用程序台词、聚会破冰活动，以及对站在她旁边的人进行实时回复。 当谈话转向一本她没有读过的书时，她会调出人工智能摘要来假装自己读完。

她并不孤单。 这种模式延伸到了一代年轻人，他们让聊天机器人控制他们的约会信息和社交互动，尤其是那些有社交焦虑的年轻人。 结果有时是显而易见的：奥斯汀私人教练安德里亚·华莱士（Andrea Wallace）注意到约会对象的短信语法突然得到改善，这是一个迹象。 西北大学学生卢卡斯·德沃拉克 (Lucas Dvorak) 的女朋友告诉他，在她身上使用人工智能感觉“令人毛骨悚然”。 20 岁的 Kalin Lincoln 使用 ChatGPT 来平息愤怒的电子邮件，并在困难的对话之前准备笔记，但她表示，这至少有一次适得其反，给了她所需的相反建议。

临床心理学家阿什利·戈尔登（Ashleigh Golden）警告说，要求人工智能检查你的短信是否“听起来不错”会悄悄地教会你不相信自己的直觉。 心理健康专家称这种模式为“自我不信任的流行病”。 关系教练亚历山德拉·弗里德曼（Alexandra Friedman）建议将人工智能排练限制为每周一次，并使用聊天机器人来决定要说什么，而不是如何说。 沃顿商学院的研究人员创造了“认知投降”来描述人们即使在人工智能是错误的情况下也会顺从它，而社会版本是同样的现象应用于人格而不是事实。 人工智能版本的你更加善于表达。 面对面的版本是必须维持对话的版本。

一项研究发现，人工智能建议的准确性降低了三倍，但自信却提高了一倍，而社交方面的相似之处是精确的：外包对话可以建立对脚本的信心，而不是对自己的信心。 避免每一个不舒服的时刻都意味着失去建立信任的机会。 聊天机器人处理最困难的部分。 焦虑仍然停留在原来的地方。
